study_identification_part.si_4_title: Judged by your neighbors: A novel framework for personalized assessment of brain structural aging effects in diverse populations

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: NAKO (German National Cohort) was used as the primary training dataset for normative model construction (N=29,883 HC). ADNI, AIBL, OASIS-3, and NIFD were used as external test datasets for evaluating biomarker efficacy in detecting neurodegenerative diseases (total N=5,857). An additional dataset MACS (Marburg-Münster Affective Disorder Cohort Study, not listed in standard categories) was used for stability analysis (N=835 HC).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Neuroimaging data from six different studies were provided by the respective consortia. Our study includes data from the German National Cohort (NAKO), the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), the Münster-Marburg Affective Disorder Cohort (MACS), the Australian Imaging, Biomarker Lifestyle Study of Aging (AIBL), the Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Neuroimaging Initiative (NIFD), and the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies 3 (OASIS3)."

answer.ADNI: external test for HC vs MCI/AD classification; also used for stability analysis (HC subset)

answer.AIBL: external test for HC vs MCI/AD classification

answer.OASIS-3: external test for HC vs MCI/AD classification

answer.NIFD: external test for HC vs FTD classification

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: NAKO (N=29,883 HC) served as the population-based training sample for all normative modeling approaches (N³, Brain Age, classical normative modeling). ADNI, AIBL, OASIS-3 provided test data with HC, MCI, and AD groups for evaluating biomarker efficacy in detecting neurodegenerative diseases. NIFD provided HC and FTD groups for FTD detection evaluation. Additionally, MACS (N=835 HC) and ADNI (N=1,073 HC) were used specifically for stability analysis of N³ models.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The training data for fitting models of the different normative modeling approaches comprised 30,047 samples from the population-based NAKO cohort... We then fit the models of the different normative model approaches using this large and diverse sample." ... "To investigate each normativity marker's effectiveness in identifying brain structural anomalies and (early) signs of neurodegeneration, additional data involving 5,857 participants were utilized, sourced from ADNI, AIBL, OASIS and NIFD datasets." ... "Validation subsets included n=835 healthy control participants from the MACS study...and an additional n=1073 healthy older adults from the ADNI study to span a wider age demographic."

model-1.model-name: N³ (Nearest Neighbor Normativity) and comparative models (Brain Age, classical normative modeling)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative reference sample from NAKO was used to train all normative modeling approaches (N³, Brain Age model, classical normative modeling). The paper states initial sample was 30,047 but after excluding age groups <22 and >72 years due to small sample sizes (n<100), the final training sample was 29,883. For the Brain Age model specifically, 90% was used for training and 10% for bias correction, but the overall reference sample remains 29,883. All models were trained on the same healthy control population.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The training data for fitting models of the different normative modeling approaches comprised 30,047 samples from the population-based NAKO cohort... We exclude age groups below 22 years and above 72 years due to small sample sizes (n < 100), which restricts the final sample to 29,883. We then fit the models of the different normative model approaches using this large and diverse sample."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics are provided in Table 2 for the NAKO training sample. The mean age was 48.45 years with SD of 12.09. The age range was restricted to 22-72 years as stated in Methods: 'participants younger than 22 years or older than 72 were omitted from the study, due to insufficient sample sizes in the normative reference sample'. No distinction between overall and train phase is made as all 29,883 samples were used for model training. Median and IQR are not reported.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Exclusion criteria were applied based on age; participants younger than 22 years or older than 72 were omitted from the study, due to insufficient sample sizes in the normative reference sample." Table 2 shows NAKO HC: "N Included: 29883, Mean Age: 48.45 ± 12.09"

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex distribution is provided in Table 2 for the NAKO training sample. Female count was 13,201 (44.18%). Male count was calculated by subtraction: 29,883 - 13,201 = 16,682. Male percentage calculated as 16,682 / 29,883 × 100 = 55.82%. No distinction between overall and train phase as all 29,883 samples were used for model training.
